summary: Adding zero on the right leaves a natural number unchanged.
detailed_explanation: For all n : Nat, the theorem Nat.add_zero proves n + 0 = n. It is a canonical identity lemma used to close arithmetic normalization goals.
research_context: Identity laws are foundational rewrite rules in mechanized arithmetic. They reduce proof search complexity by normalizing expressions early.
paper_notes: Normalization-by-rewriting with neutral elements appears in many proof assistant tactic engines and simplifier architectures.

summary: Adding zero on the left leaves a natural number unchanged.
detailed_explanation: Nat.zero_add proves 0 + n = n for all natural numbers n. It complements Nat.add_zero and is frequently used by simplification tactics.
research_context: Left/right identity symmetry is important for canonical forms in equational theorem proving.
paper_notes: Symmetric rewrite systems can improve completion and proof compression in equational logic.

summary: Introduces assumptions and quantified variables into context.
detailed_explanation: The intro tactic transforms goals like ∀ x, P x or A -> B by introducing x or a hypothesis h : A into the local context.
research_context: Context introduction corresponds to lambda abstraction and implication introduction in natural deduction.
paper_notes: Tactic-level introduction steps map directly to proof-term lambda binders in the Curry-Howard correspondence.

summary: Closes a goal with an already-matching term.
detailed_explanation: exact t succeeds when term t has the same type as the current goal. It is a direct proof-term insertion tactic.
research_context: Exact steps expose explicit proof objects, which are useful for explainability and proof artifact extraction.
paper_notes: Proof term extraction and replay rely on exact term boundaries for reproducibility.

summary: Simplifies then closes goals using rewriting.
detailed_explanation: simpa combines simplification with exact matching. It is efficient when a target theorem almost matches the goal up to definitional simplification.
research_context: Hybrid automation tactics reduce proof script length while preserving machine-checkability.
paper_notes: Simp-like rewriting strategies are central to practical Lean proof engineering.

summary: Runs a simplifier over the current goal/context.
detailed_explanation: simp applies a rewrite database to normalize expressions and discharge trivial goals.
research_context: Controlled rewriting is a core automation primitive in theorem provers.
paper_notes: Term rewriting and simplification heuristics impact proof search completeness and speed.

summary: Proves goals by reflexivity of equality.
detailed_explanation: rfl solves equalities when both sides reduce to the same term by definitional equality.
research_context: Definitional equality is checked by normalization, enabling fast proof closure for many structural equalities.
paper_notes: Definitional equality and reduction strategies are central design points in dependent type theory implementations.

summary: Builds a conjunction from separate proofs.
detailed_explanation: And.intro takes proofs of P and Q and returns a proof of P ∧ Q.
research_context: Conjunction introduction is a standard natural deduction rule used in structured proof composition.
paper_notes: Logical connective introduction/elimination rules provide interpretable proof step semantics for education tools.

summary: Proves a disjunction by proving the left branch.
detailed_explanation: Or.inl converts a proof of P into a proof of P ∨ Q.
research_context: Disjunction constructors encode branching logic in type-theoretic proofs.
paper_notes: Sum types and constructive disjunctions are tightly connected in proof assistants.

summary: Proves a disjunction by proving the right branch.
detailed_explanation: Or.inr converts a proof of Q into a proof of P ∨ Q.
research_context: Constructive disjunction requires explicit evidence for one branch.
paper_notes: Explicit constructors improve proof trace transparency in explainable theorem proving systems.
